name: Infrared Imaging & Interpretation
summary: Infrared recordings measure radiation outside visible light. Interpreting apparent brightness, shape and motion requires sensor context, calibration and geometry.

scienceResearch.intro: Infrared recordings measure radiation outside visible light. Interpreting apparent brightness, shape and motion requires sensor context, calibration and geometry.
scienceResearch.keyPrinciple: Apparent image behavior needs calibrated context before it becomes a physical measurement.
scienceResearch.keyPrincipleSupport: Established imaging principles and paper-specific hypotheses carry different evidentiary weight.

foundation.title: Beyond visible light
foundation.text: Infrared is electromagnetic radiation at longer wavelengths than visible light. Near-infrared observations can record reflected light, while thermal bands allow observation of emitted radiation.

foundation.title: Display versus object
foundation.text: An infrared picture represents detected radiation through an instrument and display. A bright feature alone does not establish its identity or a calibrated temperature.

foundation.title: Reading a recording
foundation.text: Analysts need the spectral band, calibration, timing, image scale and processing history. Avoid assuming every military video is infrared.

foundation.title: Testing brightness changes
foundation.text: The PR135 authors compare periodic brightness changes with animal recordings and test planted constant-brightness controls. Their bird interpretation remains provisional.

foundation.title: What remains unresolved?
foundation.text: A resemblance or shared frequency does not identify a species. Missing range and platform telemetry also limit physical-motion estimates.
